BaseVolatility.description:
Cheyette base volatility in decimal rate units per square-root model year.

A level of 0.005 is a 50 basis point rate amplitude. The process samples
the amplitude at the left endpoint of each step and squares it for the
variance-state drift.

CheyetteRoughVolParams.description:
Cheyette + rough stochastic volatility model parameters.

Encapsulates all inputs required to define the Cheyette dynamics with a
rough vol driver. Serialization preserves both the base-volatility curve
and initial-forward curve; deserialization validates the complete model
through the same constructor used for market inputs.

hurst.description: Hurst exponent H ∈ (0, 0.5) for the rough vol driver.

kappa.description: Mean reversion of the short rate (κ > 0).

phi_times.description: Time knots for the initial forward rate curve φ(t) = f(0, t).

phi_values.description: Value knots for the initial forward rate curve φ(t) = f(0, t).

rho.description: Correlation between rate and vol innovations ρ ∈ [-1, 1].

sigma_base.description: Base volatility term structure σ₀(t) for the rate process.

CollateralAssetClass.description:
Collateral asset classes per BCBS-IOSCO standards.

Asset classes determine baseline haircuts and eligibility criteria.
The BCBS-IOSCO framework specifies minimum haircuts by asset class.

# Reference

BCBS-IOSCO "Margin requirements for non-centrally cleared derivatives" (2020)
Annex A: Standardized haircut schedule `docs/REFERENCES.md#bcbs-iosco-uncleared-margin`

oneOf.description: Sovereign government bonds accepted as collateral.
Debt issued or guaranteed by eligible agencies.
Covered bonds meeting the applicable eligibility criteria.
Investment-grade corporate bonds accepted under the CSA.
Eligible mutual funds or exchange-traded funds.

CollateralEligibility.description:
Single collateral eligibility entry.

Defines eligibility criteria and haircut for a specific type of collateral.

concentration_limit.description:
Concentration limit as fraction of total collateral (optional)

E.g., 0.30 means max 30% of collateral can be this type.

fx_haircut_addon.description:
Additional FX haircut for currency mismatch (decimal)

Applied when collateral currency differs from settlement currency.

min_rating.description:
Minimum credit rating requirement (e.g., "A-", "BBB")

If None, no rating constraint applies.

CsaSpec.description:
Credit Support Annex specification (ISDA standard).

The CSA governs the exchange of collateral between counterparties
for OTC derivatives. This specification captures all key commercial
terms needed for margin calculation and management.

# ISDA Documentation

This type represents terms from:
- ISDA 2016 Credit Support Annex for Variation Margin (VM CSA)
- ISDA 2018 Credit Support Annex for Initial Margin (IM CSA)

# References

- ISDA 2016 VM CSA: `docs/REFERENCES.md#isda-vm-csa-2016`
- ISDA 2018 IM CSA: `docs/REFERENCES.md#isda-im-csa-2018`
- BCBS-IOSCO uncleared margin framework: `docs/REFERENCES.md#bcbs-iosco-uncleared-margin`

# Example

```
use finstack_quant_margin::types::{CsaSpec, VmParameters, ImParameters, EligibleCollateralSchedule, MarginCallTiming, ImMethodology, MarginTenor};
use finstack_quant_core::currency::Currency;
use finstack_quant_core::money::Money;

# fn main() -> finstack_quant_core::Result<()> {
let csa = CsaSpec {
    id: "USD-CSA-2024".to_string(),
    base_currency: Currency::USD,
    vm_params: VmParameters::regulatory_standard(Currency::USD)?,
    im_params: Some(ImParameters::for_methodology(finstack_quant_margin::types::ImMethodology::Simm, Currency::USD)?),
    eligible_collateral: EligibleCollateralSchedule::bcbs_standard()?,
    call_timing: MarginCallTiming::regulatory_standard()?,
    collateral_curve_id: "USD-OIS".into(),
    calendar_id: "usny".into(),
};
# Ok(())
# }
```

Base currency for margin calculations.

All exposures and collateral values are converted to this currency
for netting and comparison with thresholds.

calendar_id.description: Contractual business-day calendar for calls and settlements.

collateral_curve_id.description:
Discount curve ID for collateral valuation.

Cash collateral is typically discounted at OIS/RFR rates.
This curve should match the CSA's collateral interest rate.

eligible_collateral.description:
Eligible collateral schedule.

Defines what collateral types are acceptable and associated haircuts.

im_params.description:
Initial margin parameters (optional).

If None, no IM is exchanged (either not in scope for regulations
or trade is cleared).

vm_params.description:
Variation margin parameters.

Governs daily mark-to-market collateral exchange.

Identifies which family of curve an operation targets.

These variants map to the market data collections exposed by

They also determine which quoting and interpolation conventions apply when

# Examples
```rust

let kind = CurveKind::Discount;
assert_eq!(format!("{:?}", kind), "Discount");
```

Price shocks use [`OperationSpec::CommodityCurveParallelPct`] or

default_haircut.description:
Default haircut for unlisted collateral (if accepted)

If None, only explicitly listed collateral types are accepted.

rehypothecation_allowed.description:
Whether rehypothecation of posted collateral is permitted

For IM under BCBS-IOSCO rules, rehypothecation is prohibited.
For VM, rehypothecation may be permitted by bilateral agreement.

Settled cash at the valuation cut before the first modeled call.

discount_curve_id.description: Explicit discount dependency when the curve's shock recipe requires it.

FbmSpec.description:
Generator of the fractional increments consumed by `rough_bergomi` and
`cheyette_rough`.

Serialized as an internally tagged object: `{"type": "volterra"}`. The
Hurst exponent always comes from the process parameters.

Only `volterra` reproduces the published models: both are defined on the
Riemann-Liouville Volterra process, whose increments are not stationary.
`cholesky` and `windowed_conditional` drive the same recursion with true
fractional Brownian motion instead. Forwards are unchanged. Exact
fractional Brownian motion has the same marginal variance `t^(2H)`, so the
expected variance is unchanged too, but its autocovariance differs, so
smiles and path statistics differ. The windowed generator only
approximates the level variance once the path is longer than its window,
which biases the expected variance.

The variants without settings are written `FbmSpec::Volterra {}` so that
the tagged object rejects unknown keys.

# References

- Hybrid scheme: `docs/REFERENCES.md#bennedsen-lunde-pakkanen-2017`
- Rough Bergomi: `docs/REFERENCES.md#bayer-friz-gatheral-2016`

oneOf.description:
Riemann-Liouville Volterra increments from the Bennedsen-Lunde-Pakkanen
hybrid scheme. Needs an equally spaced time grid. `O(n²)` work per path
in the number of steps `n`.

Exact fractional Brownian motion increments from the Cholesky factor
of their covariance. Any time grid. `O(n³)` setup, `O(n²)` storage and
work per path; limited to 8,000 steps.

Approximate fractional Brownian motion increments: exact for the first
`near_field_size` steps, then each increment is drawn conditionally on
the previous `near_field_size` increments only. Any time grid.
`O(n · near_field_size)` work per path.

near_field_size.description:
Positive window length in steps, capped at the number of steps.
Omitted selects `min(max(10, √n), 50)`.

ForwardVarianceCurve.description:
Forward variance curve ξ₀(t) for rough volatility models.

Represents `ξ₀(t) = E^Q[V_t | F₀]`, expected instantaneous variance under
the consuming model's pricing measure. Values are supplied or calibrated by
the caller. The integral sets the model's expected accumulated variance.

Differencing ATM implied total variance is an optional proxy, not an exact
variance-swap bootstrap. This type interpolates the supplied curve; it does
not perform market calibration.

interpolation.description: Interpolation contract used by the constructor.

times.description: Point times or interval ends (strictly increasing year fractions).

values.description: Point samples or constant interval variances (all nonnegative).

HurstExponent.description:
Validated Hurst exponent H ∈ (0, 1).

The Hurst exponent determines the roughness of fractional Brownian motion:

- H < 0.5 — rough (anti-persistent increments)
- H = 0.5 — standard Brownian motion
- H > 0.5 — more regular paths with persistent increments

ImMethodology.description:
Initial margin calculation methodology.

Different methodologies are used depending on regulatory requirements,
product type, and whether trades are cleared or bilateral.

# BCBS-IOSCO Standards

For bilateral (uncleared) OTC derivatives, either SIMM or the regulatory
schedule approach may be used. SIMM is the industry standard for large
dealers due to its risk-sensitivity.

oneOf.description:
Haircut-based IM calculation (standard for repos and securities financing)

IM = Collateral_Value × Haircut

Haircuts are determined by asset class, rating, maturity, and FX mismatch.

ISDA Standard Initial Margin Model (SIMM)

Sensitivities-based model calculating IM from delta, vega, and curvature
risk across interest rate, credit, equity, commodity, and FX risk classes.

Reference: ISDA SIMM Methodology v2.6 (2023)

BCBS-IOSCO regulatory schedule approach

Grid-based IM calculation using notional × rate based on asset class and maturity.
Simpler but typically more conservative than SIMM.

Example rates:
- Interest Rate: 0-2yr: 1%, 2-5yr: 2%, 5+yr: 4%
- Credit: 2-5yr: 5%, 5+yr: 10%
- Equity: 15%
- FX: 6%

Internal model approved by regulator

Bank's proprietary VaR or ES-based model approved by supervisor.
Must meet regulatory backtesting and validation requirements.

Clearing house methodology

CCP-specific IM calculation (typically VaR or SPAN-based).
Examples: LCH SwapClear, CME, ICE Clear Credit

ImParameters.description:
Initial margin parameters.

Initial margin is collateral posted to cover potential future exposure (PFE)
during the close-out period following a default. IM is required for
non-centrally cleared derivatives under BCBS-IOSCO rules.

# Margin Period of Risk (MPOR)

The MPOR determines the horizon over which PFE is calculated:
- Standard: 10 business days for bilateral derivatives
- Reduced: 5 days for certain liquid products

# Example

```
use finstack_quant_margin::types::{ImMethodology, ImParameters};
use finstack_quant_core::currency::Currency;
use finstack_quant_core::money::Money;

let im_params = ImParameters {
    methodology: ImMethodology::Simm,
    mpor_days: 10,
    threshold: Money::from((50_000_000_i64, Currency::USD)),
    mta: Money::from((0_i64, Currency::USD)), // Combined with VM MTA
    segregated: true,
};
```

methodology.description:
IM calculation methodology.

Options include SIMM, regulatory schedule, or CCP methodology.

mpor_days.description:
Margin Period of Risk in business days.

Standard is 10 days under BCBS-IOSCO. CCPs may use shorter periods.

mta.description:
Minimum Transfer Amount for IM.

Combined IM+VM MTA must not exceed €500,000 under BCBS-IOSCO.

segregated.description:
Whether IM must be held in a segregated account.

Under BCBS-IOSCO, IM must be segregated with a third-party custodian
to protect it in case of the collecting party's insolvency.

threshold.description:
Group-level IM threshold allocated to this CSA by the caller.

BCBS-IOSCO permits €50M aggregate threshold at group level.
Many large dealers operate with zero threshold by agreement.

expiries.description: Expiry axis in years, strictly increasing and non-negative.

local_vols.description:
Local volatilities as annualized decimals, finite and non-negative,
row-major: `local_vols[expiry_index * strikes.len() + strike_index]`.

strikes.description:
Strike axis in price units of the underlying, strictly increasing and
positive.

MarginCallTiming.description:
Margin call timing parameters.

Specifies the operational timing for margin calls including
notification and dispute resolution windows.

delivery_grace_days.description: Grace period for collateral delivery (business days)

notification_deadline_hours.description: Notification deadline (hours after valuation, e.g., 13:00 local time)

MarginTenor.description:
Margin call frequency.

Determines how often margin calls are made and collateral is exchanged.
Industry standard for OTC derivatives is daily under BCBS-IOSCO rules.

oneOf.description: Daily margin calls (standard for OTC derivatives post-2016)
On-demand margin calls (used for repos and some bilateral agreements)

MaturityConstraints.description:
Maturity constraints for eligible collateral.

Some CSAs restrict collateral based on remaining maturity to limit
duration risk in the collateral portfolio.

max_remaining_years.description: Maximum remaining years to maturity (if any)

min_remaining_years.description: Minimum remaining years to maturity (if any)

amount.description:
Monetary amount, carried on the wire as an exact decimal string rather
than a JSON number so no precision is lost in transit. Construction with
configuration applies the selected ingest scale; raw construction does not.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency of `amount`. Arithmetic between two `Money` values
requires this to match; there is no implicit conversion.

NettingSetId.description:
Identifies a margin netting set.

Instruments in the same netting set can offset each other for margin
calculation purposes. The netting set is typically defined by the
CSA agreement (bilateral) or by CCP membership (cleared) — these two
shapes are mutually exclusive, so the type encodes them as enum
variants rather than as a struct with two `Option<String>` fields
that could in principle both be set or both be unset.

oneOf.description: A bilateral netting set scoped by counterparty + CSA.
A cleared netting set scoped by CCP membership.

ccp_id.description: CCP identifier (also used as the counterparty id)

PathSimulationSpec.description: Complete, serializable description of one path simulation.

antithetic.description:
Emit an antithetic partner after each path, driven by the negated
normal draws of the same stream.

initial_state.description:
State at time zero, in the layout documented on the [`ProcessSpec`]
variant. Heston and rough Heston take only spot here and use their
own `v0` for the starting variance.

num_paths.description:
Number of independent random streams, in `1..=100_000`. Each stream
yields one path, or two when `antithetic` is set.

scheme.description: Discretization scheme; defaults to the process's canonical scheme.

seed.description:
Root seed of the Philox generator. The same spec always reproduces the
same paths bit for bit.

ProcessSpec.description:
Stochastic process to simulate, with its parameters.

Serialized as an internally tagged object: `{"type": "gbm", "r": 0.03, ...}`.
Parameters are re-validated when [`simulate_paths`] runs, so a spec read
from JSON cannot bypass the range checks of the Rust constructors.

oneOf.description:
Geometric Brownian motion `dS = (r - q) S dt + σ S dW`.

State: `[spot]`, which must start strictly positive.

Geometric Brownian motion with discrete dividends paid at fixed times.

State: `[spot]`, which must start strictly positive.

dividends.description:
Dividend schedule as `[time, dividend]` pairs. `time` is the
ex-dividend time in years: strictly positive and distinct, in any
order. A cash dividend is a non-negative amount in spot units and
a proportional dividend a non-negative decimal fraction of spot.

params.description:
Diffusion parameters between dividend dates. Set `q` to zero when
every dividend is listed explicitly.

oneOf.description:
Correlated geometric Brownian motions, one per asset.

State: `[spot_0, spot_1, ...]`, each starting strictly positive.

assets.description: Per-asset parameters; the vector length is the state dimension.

correlation.description:
Row-major `n x n` correlation matrix of the driving Brownian
motions; omitted means independent assets.

oneOf.description:
Arithmetic Brownian motion with drift `dX = μ dt + σ dW`.

State: `[x]`.

sigma.description: Constant diffusion scale per square root year.

oneOf.description:
Correlated arithmetic Brownian motions.

State: `[x_0, x_1, ...]`.

correlation.description:
Row-major `n x n` correlation matrix of the driving Brownian
motions; omitted means independent components.

mus.description:
Per-component drifts per year; the vector length is the state
dimension.

sigmas.description: Per-component diffusion scales per square-root year, non-negative.

oneOf.description:
Correlated Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes `dX_i = κ_i (θ_i - X_i) dt + σ_i dW_i`.

State: `[x_0, x_1, ...]`.

correlation.description: Optional row-major `n x n` correlation matrix.

sigmas.description: Diffusion scales `σ_i` per square root year.

oneOf.description:
Hull-White one-factor short rate `dr = κ (θ(t) - r) dt + σ(t) dW`.

State: `[short_rate]` as a decimal.

Cox-Ingersoll-Ross square-root process `dv = κ (θ - v) dt + σ √v dW`.

State: `[short_rate]` (or an intensity or variance), starting
non-negative.

CIR++ short rate `r_t = x_t + φ(t)` with `x` a CIR factor and `φ` a
piecewise-constant deterministic shift.

State: `[short_rate]`. The initial state is the short rate `r_0`, not
the factor: the factor starts at `r_0 - φ(0)`, which must be
non-negative, and every reported value is the shifted rate.

params.description: Parameters of the unshifted CIR factor.

shift_curve.description:
Shift values `φ` as decimal rates, one per entry of `shift_times`;
each applies from its time until the next.

shift_times.description:
Strictly increasing shift start times in years. Times before the
first entry use the first shift value.

oneOf.description:
Heston stochastic volatility.

Supply only the strictly positive opening spot in `initial_state`.
The process derives variance from its `v0` parameter and returns states
as `[spot, variance]`.

q.description: Continuously compounded dividend or foreign yield as an annual decimal.

r.description: Continuously compounded risk-free rate as an annual decimal.

oneOf.description:
Schwartz-Smith two-factor commodity model.

State: `[x, y]`, the short-term deviation and the long-term level of
the log price; the spot is `exp(x + y)`.

kappa.description: Mean reversion speed for short-term deviation (κ_X)

lambda_x.description:
Constant risk-premium drift shift for the short-term factor (λ_X).

Under the risk-neutral measure the short-term factor follows
`dX = (−κ_X X − λ_X) dt + σ_X dW*` (Schwartz & Smith 2000): a constant
drift shift at unchanged κ_X. Defaults to 0 (physical measure).

oneOf.description:
Dupire local volatility `dS = (r - q) S dt + σ_loc(t, S) S dW`, with
`σ_loc` read from a local volatility surface at the simulation time
and the current spot.

State: `[spot]`, which must start strictly positive. The default
scheme is `log_euler`; its discretization error falls with the step
size, so use a fine time grid (about 100 steps per year).

q.description:
Dividend yield or foreign rate, continuously compounded (annualized
decimal).

surface.description:
Local volatility `σ_loc(t, S)`: expiry axis in years from the
simulation start, strike axis in spot price units. Flat outside its
grid.

oneOf.description:
LIBOR market model: displaced-lognormal forward rates under the
terminal measure, with piecewise-constant factor loadings.

State: `[forward_0, forward_1, ...]`, simple forward rates as decimals,
one per accrual period. `initial_state` must equal the
`initial_forwards` parameter. A forward stops moving at its fixing
date, and the time grid must contain every fixing date and volatility
breakpoint inside the horizon.

accrual_factors.description: Accrual factors τ_i = T_{i+1} − T_i (length N).

displacements.description: Displacement per forward for negative-rate support (length N).

initial_forwards.description: Initial forward rates F_i(0) from the curve (length N).

tenors.description: Tenor dates T_0, T_1, ..., T_N (N+1 dates, year fractions).

vol_values.description:
Factor loadings λ_{i,k}(t) per forward, per time period.

Outer: M+1 time periods.
Inner: N forwards, each with up to 3 factor loadings.

oneOf.description:
Rough Bergomi stochastic volatility: lognormal variance driven by a
Riemann-Liouville Volterra process, around the forward variance curve
`xi`.

State: `[spot]`, which must start strictly positive. The variance is a
functional of the driver's history and is not part of the state.
Consumes fractional noise; see [`FbmSpec`].

hurst.description: Hurst exponent H ∈ (0, 0.5), typically 0.07–0.12 for equity indices.

oneOf.description:
Rough Heston stochastic volatility: a Volterra square-root variance
with a power-law kernel, `hurst` in `(0, 0.5)`.

Supply only the strictly positive opening spot in `initial_state`.
The process derives variance from its `v0` parameter and returns states
as `[spot, variance]`.
At most 8,000 steps.

hurst.description: Hurst exponent H ∈ (0, 0.5) — controls the roughness of the variance.

oneOf.description:
Cheyette short-rate model with rough stochastic volatility.

`sigma_base` holds point or ending-interval amplitudes in decimal rate
units per square-root model year. For example, a flat 50 bp amplitude
is `{"interpolation":"linear","amplitudes":[[0.0,0.005]]}`.

State: `[x, y]`, the deviation of the short rate from the initial
forward curve and the accumulated variance; both normally start at
zero. The short rate at time `t` is `x + φ(t)`, with `φ` the initial
forward curve in the parameters. Consumes fractional noise; see
[`FbmSpec`].

SchemeSpec.description: Time-discretization scheme used to advance the process.

oneOf.description:
The process's canonical scheme: its exact transition where one exists,
quadratic-exponential for square-root variance, Euler otherwise. See
the [module table](self#supported-pairs).

Euler on the log state, which keeps the state positive. Only for
`gbm`, `multi_gbm` and `local_vol`.

Milstein with the proportional-diffusion correction
`½ σ² X (Z² - 1) Δt`. Only for `gbm` and `multi_gbm`.

TimeGridSpec.description: Simulation dates, as year fractions from the simulation start.

times.description:
Strictly increasing finite times in years, starting at exactly
`0.0`, with at least two entries.

VmParameters.description:
Variation margin parameters.

These parameters govern the daily (or periodic) exchange of variation margin
under a CSA agreement. VM is exchanged to eliminate mark-to-market exposure.

# ISDA CSA Standard Terms

The 2016 VM CSA introduced standardized terms for variation margin:
- Zero threshold for in-scope entities
- Daily exchange with T+1 settlement
- Cash or highly liquid securities as collateral

# Example

```
use finstack_quant_margin::types::{MarginTenor, VmParameters};
use finstack_quant_core::currency::Currency;
use finstack_quant_core::money::Money;

let vm_params = VmParameters {
    threshold: Money::from((10_000_000_i64, Currency::USD)),
    mta: Money::from((500_000_i64, Currency::USD)),
    rounding: Money::from((10_000_i64, Currency::USD)),
    independent_amount: Money::from((0_i64, Currency::USD)),
    frequency: MarginTenor::Daily,
    settlement_lag: 1,
};
```

frequency.description:
Margin call frequency.

Under BCBS-IOSCO, daily margin exchange is required.

independent_amount.description:
Independent Amount (IA) / Additional Margin.

Fixed collateral amount required regardless of exposure.
Often used for credit enhancement or as a buffer.

mta.description:
Minimum Transfer Amount (MTA).

Margin calls below MTA are not made. BCBS-IOSCO permits combined
IM+VM MTA up to €500,000 equivalent.

rounding.description:
Rounding increment for margin amounts.

Margin calls are typically rounded to the nearest multiple of this amount.

settlement_lag.description:
Settlement lag in business days (T+n).

Standard is T+1 for VM under 2016 VM CSA.

threshold.description:
Threshold amount below which no margin is exchanged.

Under BCBS-IOSCO rules for covered entities, VM threshold must be zero.
Legacy bilateral CSAs may have non-zero thresholds.

description: Dated simulated market states, factor mappings, legal scope and optional cash collateral.

cash_vm.description:
Elected cash variation margin with scheduled calls, settlements and
collateral interest. Omit for an uncollateralized calculation.

dates.description: Observation calendar dates, including the portfolio valuation date.

factors.description: Explicit selection and units of each market factor to simulate.

netting_set.description: Structural counterparty and agreement scope for the supplied positions.

netting_source_id.description: Identifier of the authoritative record admitting the supplied book.

position_ids.description: Exact position IDs in that netting record, qualified as one eligible set.

simulation.description:
Process initialized against the held market. Its explicit grid must equal
the ACT/365 Fixed observation dates. Unmapped state channels remain
internal to the process, such as variance driving the equity spot.

title: ExposureSimulationConfig
